history.summary: CSV town 'Mysore' is correct (temple within the Mysore Palace complex, near the north gate). The Sri Bhuvaneshwari Temple was commissioned in 1951 by Maharaja Jayachamaraja Wodeyar and built in the traditional Dravidian style with a Chola-style gateway. The principal deity, Goddess Bhuvaneshwari, and the other sculptures (Surya, Maha Vishnu, Maheshwara, Rajarajeshwari, Ganapati, Chamundeshwari) were carved by the noted Mysore sculptor Siddalingaswamy. A highlight is the large copper Surya Mandala gifted by the Maharaja, which receives special pooja every year on Ratha Saptami. Coordinates are geocoder-level approximations for the palace north-gate area.

name: Sri Bhuvaneshwari Temple
town_description: Mysuru (Mysore), Karnataka's 'City of Palaces', was the historic capital of the Wodeyar dynasty and remains one of South India's major heritage destinations, anchored by the Mysore Palace and Chamundi Hills. The city is renowned for its Dussehra festival, silk, sandalwood, and the cluster of temples inside the palace premises. The Bhuvaneshwari temple stands near the palace's north gate on Albert Victor Road, visited by palace tourists.
